The Blandford School is a vibrant, inclusive, and ambitious community at the heart of Blandford.
It is our pleasure to welcome you to The Blandford School. We are incredibly proud of our school at the heart of our vibrant and supportive community. We are deeply committed to providing an education that not only inspires our young people academically, but also nurtures their confidence, character, and wellbeing.
At The Blandford School, we believe that every child deserves the very best start in life. This means offering an ambitious and enriching curriculum while ensuring that each student receives the pastoral support they need to thrive. Our staff work tirelessly to balance high expectations with genuine care, ensuring that students feel valued, safe, and motivated to achieve their personal best.
Our REAP values – Respect, Effort, Attitude and Perseverance – sit at the core of everything we do. These values shape the culture of our school and help our students grow into responsible, thoughtful, and ambitious young adults. We take great pride in promoting our values every day, recognising students not only for what they achieve, but for the positive contribution they make to our community.
We are passionate about providing opportunities for every young person in Blandford and the surrounding area. Whether through academic challenge, creative and performing arts, sport, leadership experiences, or wider enrichment, we strive to ensure that every student can discover their strengths and pursue their aspirations.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website. I hope it gives you a sense of the warmth, ambition, and pride that define The Blandford School. We look forward to working in partnership with our families and community as we continue to support our young people in becoming the very best versions of themselves.

Sixth Form Open Evening – A Truly Incredible Night at The Blandford School
Our Sixth Form Open Evening last night was nothing short of spectacular. We were delighted to welcome an exceptional number of visitors—both from within The Blandford School community and from many neighbouring schools. The hall was filled to standing room only even before the first presentation began, setting the tone for an inspiring and vibrant evening.
A special congratulations must go to our outstanding Head Students, Abbie and William, along with Year 12 student Amelie, who each delivered heartfelt and confident speeches to a packed audience. Their honesty, professionalism, and courage in sharing their stories exemplified everything we are so proud of within our Sixth Form.
We have already received some truly wonderful feedback from families who attended. One parent wrote:
“I attended with my daughter, the Sixth Form Open Event this evening and I would just like to pass on, to ALL those involved, how grateful I am for such a welcoming, informative and friendly experience it was. To the Sixth Form speakers at the introduction in the Hall (so well done, it takes a lot of courage to stand up and speak to a sizeable crowd with the poise and professionalism they achieved), the current Sixth Form students who were so helpful and informative in their respective subject classrooms and to all the tutors and staff giving up their time to engage with everyone in such a positive and vibrant manner. Thank you, it was a valuable visit.”
Our heartfelt thanks go to every student and member of staff who played a role in making the evening such a success. Their enthusiasm, guidance, and warmth created an atmosphere that truly showcased what makes our Sixth Form exceptional.
To explore the wide range of opportunities available, please visit our Curriculum Options page:
👉 Sixth Form Curriculum Options — blandfordschool.org.uk/sixth-form/curriculum-options/
If you attended the event, we would love to hear your thoughts:
👉 Leave Feedback — Feedback Form
We are incredibly excited for the future of our Sixth Form and look forward to welcoming the next generation of students who will continue to shape its success. 🌟

We Will Rock You – A Show-Stopping Success!
On Tuesday 22nd and Wednesday 23rd October, The Blandford School’s Performing Arts Department wowed audiences with two incredible performances of We Will Rock You. The energy, passion, and talent displayed by our students across both nights were simply outstanding, with every song, dance, and scene delivered with confidence and flair.
Audience feedback has been overwhelmingly positive, with one audience member writing:
“Just wanted to say how all 5 of us were so impressed with the whole show!! Main characters were fantastic! Absolute credit to you!! You all deserve a medal, you must be so proud of them all!”
Both nights were filled with eager audiences, and the atmosphere in the hall was electric as our young performers brought Queen’s iconic music to life.
A huge congratulations to everyone involved — the cast, crew, band, and staff — for creating such a memorable and professional production. You have made the entire school community incredibly proud.

Sports Day 2026
A Fantastic Celebration of Competition and House Spirit
Students at The Blandford School enjoyed a brilliant Sports Day filled with determination, teamwork and plenty of house spirit.
The event saw students from Lacy (Green), Beaumont (Blue), Montfort (Yellow) and Lancaster (Red) compete across a range of track and field events, with everyone showing fantastic effort, perseverance and support for their teammates.
From sprint races and relays to field events, students embraced the challenge and represented their houses with pride. The atmosphere throughout the day was fantastic, with students encouraging each other and celebrating each other's achievements.
Congratulations go to Lancaster House, who were crowned our 2026 Sports Day Champions following an excellent day of competition.
There were further celebrations for Montfort House, who achieved the highest number of points across all house competitions throughout the academic year and were named our Overall House Points Champions. This is a fantastic achievement and recognises the continued commitment, teamwork and participation of students across the year.
A huge thank you goes to all of the staff who organised and supported the event, our student leaders who helped throughout the day, and every student who took part and made it such a memorable occasion.
We would also like to say a special thank you to Rob Young Images, who kindly gave up his time to photograph the day completely free of charge. Rob captured some fantastic moments that showcase the energy, enthusiasm and enjoyment of Sports Day. We are incredibly grateful for his support and generosity.
Please enjoy a selection of photographs from the day.

Headteacher’s Welcome
The Blandford School is a vibrant, warm, and successful community school set within beautiful grounds, in the heart of the Blandford community. We are proud to serve our local area by providing students with the very best educational start in life.
Our mission is clear: to help every student achieve the highest outcomes they are capable of, while developing the independence, confidence, and skills they need to thrive in life beyond the school gates. We believe education is a partnership between school, students, and family — and together, we create the conditions for success.
We are proud of our many significant strengths. Our GCSE results consistently exceed national averages, and our Sixth Form outcomes rank among the best in the country. Beyond the classroom, we offer a rich and varied programme of extra-curricular activities and a dynamic super curriculum at Key Stage 5, ensuring students have opportunities to explore their interests and talents.
At the heart of our approach is a commitment to high standards and clear expectations — full school uniform, excellent attendance and punctuality, and a keen focus on learning.
We believe in celebrating progress and achievement, and we use educational research to shape teaching and learning, systems and structures that support every learner. Our students understand the importance of their role in their own success: they are expected to attend punctually, engage fully in their learning, and take responsibility for their choices, actions and approach to education.
We also recognise the vital role families play. When school and home work in partnership, we create consistency and clarity for young people — helping them to flourish both academically and personally.
We are proud to have a highly skilled and dedicated team of teachers and support staff at The Blandford School. Their experience, commitment, and deep connection to our school community are central to our continued success. We place great value on professional development, drawing on the latest educational research to continually evolve our practice and ensure we provide the very best learning experiences for all our students.
We have excellent facilities and believe that school should be a place where both students and staff thrive — where learning is inspiring, relationships are strong, and everyone feels part of a collective effort. These are exciting times at The Blandford School, and we look forward to welcoming you and sharing the next evolution of our school.
Mr Alan Jones - Headteacher

A Royal Visit to Remember
Thursday 16 July was a memorable day for Blandford Forum as His Majesty King Charles III and Her Majesty Queen Camilla visited the town, celebrating its rich heritage, thriving community and recent regeneration projects.
The Blandford School was proud to be represented by Headteacher, Mr Jones, and five students, who were invited to join pupils from across the Blandford Schools Network to welcome Their Majesties.
The royal visit included a tour of the recently renovated Corn Exchange, a visit to the historic Hall & Woodhouse Brewery, and the opportunity to meet a wide range of local businesses and community organisations at a specially arranged farmers' market.
Among those showcasing their work were Sweetpea Florist, From Dorset With Love, and The Book & Bucket Cheese Company – all of which have strong links to The Blandford School through families whose children attend the school. It was wonderful to see members of our wider school community playing such an important role in the day's celebrations and proudly representing the very best of local enterprise.
Our students were delighted to be part of this special occasion, representing the school with confidence and pride while joining the community in giving Their Majesties a warm Blandford welcome.
It was a fantastic day that highlighted the strength of our local community, celebrated the success of local businesses, and showcased everything that makes Blandford Forum such a special place to live, work and learn.

Students Inspired at The Blandford School's First Ever Careers Fair
The Blandford School was delighted to welcome more than 35 employers, universities, colleges, charities, public services and training providers to our first ever Careers Fair, giving students an exciting opportunity to explore the wide range of pathways available after school.
Throughout the day, students from across the school met with exhibitors, asked thoughtful questions and discovered opportunities in higher education, apprenticeships, further education and a huge variety of careers. The Main Hall was buzzing with conversation as students explored future possibilities and made valuable connections.
The event was a fantastic success and has already received outstanding feedback from exhibitors.
The Royal Signals Corps Engagement Team described it as:
"One of the best careers fairs attended this year for our team."
They praised the event for being exceptionally well organised, highlighting the smooth arrival and set-up process, the clear table layout and the welcoming atmosphere. They also commented on the support provided by staff throughout the day and were particularly impressed by our students, describing them as polite, engaged and asking excellent questions.
The team noted how refreshing it was to meet so many students – including those in Year 9 – who already had clear ideas about their future career aspirations. They also said the event provided an excellent opportunity to showcase the careers available within their organisation.
When asked what could be improved, they simply replied that there was nothing to suggest, apart from the heat, which was beyond anyone's control!
They have already confirmed they would be delighted to return for future Careers Fairs and are keen to support The Blandford School with careers talks, workplace visits, work experience, mock interviews and STEM workshops.
They concluded their feedback by saying:
"Keep up the good work. The school was very accommodating."
A Huge Thank You to Our Exhibitors
We are incredibly grateful to every organisation that gave up their time to support our students. Their enthusiasm, advice and willingness to share their experiences made the day such a success.
Our exhibitors included:
Lancaster University
Bournemouth University
Arts University Bournemouth
University of Exeter
Bournemouth & Poole College
Dorset Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
Southern Gas Networks
Spetisbury Construction
Parker Filtration Group
Royal Corps of Signals
Dorset County Football Association
A huge thank you also goes to our Careers Team and everyone involved in organising the event and to all the staff who helped make the day run so smoothly.
Following such a positive first Careers Fair, we're already looking forward to making next year's event even bigger and better, continuing to inspire our students as they prepare for their futures.

Students Return from Inspiring Berlin Trip
Students from The Blandford School have returned safely from an exciting and educational trip to Berlin, arriving back in the early hours of Sunday morning after several packed days exploring the German capital.
The group embraced every opportunity to discover the city’s rich history and culture, averaging an impressive 25,000 steps each day as they visited many of Berlin’s most significant landmarks. Highlights included the Berlin Wall Memorial, the Brandenburg Gate and the iconic TV Tower, where students enjoyed panoramic views across the city. They also visited the popular Ritter Sport Chocolate Museum, adding a fun and memorable stop to the itinerary.
Throughout the trip, students conducted themselves exceptionally well, consistently demonstrating our REAP values — Respect, Effort, Attitude and Perseverance. Their maturity, enthusiasm and positive attitude made them a credit to both themselves and the school.
The school would like to extend its sincere thanks to Miss Davidson, Miss Ward, Miss Maclaine, Mr Smith, Mr Fenton and Mr Vairy for their hard work in organising and leading the visit. Their dedication ensured the trip ran smoothly and provided students with an unforgettable learning experience.
The Berlin trip proved to be both enriching and enjoyable, offering students valuable insights into history, culture, and life beyond the classroom.

The Big Bang 2025 – A Spectacular Night!
The Blandford School’s Big Bang Fireworks Night on Friday 7th November 2025 was a truly spectacular event, bringing together our local community for an evening of dazzling fireworks and a fantastic soundtrack. Despite the wet weather, the atmosphere was electric, and we were thrilled to welcome over 1,800 attendees!

A huge thank you to all the staff volunteers whose hard work and dedication made the evening possible, and to The Replicas for entertaining the crowd despite the rain. Special thanks also to DP Marquees for lending us a Chinese hat tent to keep the band dry.
📸 Local photographer Rob Young captured some stunning moments from the night – you can see more of his work at ryimages.co.uk.
All the money raised will go towards extra opportunities for our students, with the grand total coming soon. If you are a company and would like to help sponsor a future event or please contact abutler@blandfordschool.org.uk.

Working Together When Concerns Arise
From time to time, we all encounter situations that feel important enough to raise beyond a simple email or phone call. This is a normal part of school life, and when it happens, our aim is always to work collaboratively and constructively with families to find a positive way forward.
To achieve this, it is vital that we approach these conversations calmly and respectfully, seeking to understand the different perspectives involved. By remaining open to discussion, sharing information appropriately, and recognising the role each of us plays, we can move towards outcomes that genuinely support our young people.
If a family feels the need to escalate a concern, we kindly ask that this is done through the school’s Complaints Policy, once informal approaches have not led to a satisfactory resolution. This policy outlines a clear and recognised process for raising and reviewing concerns and can be found in the Policies section of our school website.
We appreciate your partnership in helping us maintain a supportive, respectful, and solution-focused environment for our whole school community
DFE / Ofsted Complaints
We are aware that families are not always fully informed about what happens when a concern or complaint is raised directly with the DfE or Ofsted. A common assumption is that an inspector—or a representative from one of these organisations—will immediately visit the school, carry out a detailed investigation, and that the school may face sanctions as a result.
It is important to clarify that this is not how the process works.
In most cases, the DfE or Ofsted will ask the Local Authority and/or the school to provide further information through what is known as a seeking assurances process. This involves reviewing the details provided by both parties to understand the situation more clearly. It is largely an administrative check to ensure that appropriate procedures have been followed, rather than an external inspection or punitive measure.
If at any point you feel that your concern has not been fully heard, we strongly encourage you to use our published Complaints Policy, which sets out a clear and recognised escalation route. This process ensures that concerns are addressed fairly, transparently, and with the aim of reaching an appropriate resolution for everyone involved.
We appreciate your cooperation and continued partnership in working together for the benefit of our school community.

Signposting for support
At The Blandford School, we understand that life can sometimes be challenging, and it’s important to know where to turn for help. This page brings together a range of trusted resources and links to support you and your family across a variety of areas, including mental health, children’s social care, local services, online safety, parenting guidance, financial support, sexual health, school attendance, and recommended books.
Whether you’re looking for advice, practical help, or just someone to talk to, these links connect you with the right people and organisations to provide support when you need it.
Mental Health Support
MHST https://camhsdorset.org/about-camhs/mental-health-support-teams-mhsts
MHST work in school to tackle the challenges children and young people experience, by helping them to feel more resilient, arming them with techniques to look after themselves and strategies to help them cope better with life’s ups and downs. This includes support for things like mild-moderate anxiety or worries, exam stress and friendship issues through 6-8 sessions of low intensity Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (LI-CBT), counselling sessions, themed group work or information workshops. We also been support the transition between schools and have been working with the year 6 classes going up into year 7.
The MHST and The Blandford School work closely together to provide support to students. To start the referral process, please email your child’s Head of Year to share an update on your child’s current situation and the reasons you feel support is needed, including any relevant information regarding their safety. As part of the referral, the MHST will also ask The Blandford School to provide your child’s most recent attendance information and their SEND status, to ensure MHST is the right service at this time.
Find out more here: MHST Video for Parents/Carers
Access resources here:
MHST Resources for Parents/Carers
CAMHS https://camhsdorset.org/parents-carers/parents-of-teenagers
CAMHS provides support to children and young people who are coping with significant mental health difficulties. Find out what we help with – and how
Kooth https://www.kooth.com/
Kooth is your online mental wellbeing community. Access is free, safe and anonymous. Developed and monitored by Mental Health professionals
Childline https://www.childline.org.uk/
Childline is here to help anyone under 19 in the UK with any issue they’re going through. You can talk about anything. Whether it’s something big or small, our trained counsellors are here to support you.
Childline is free, confidential and available any time, day or night. You can talk to us:
by calling 0800 1111
through 1-2-1 counsellor chat
Beat Eating Disorders https://www.beateatingdisorders.org.uk/about-beat/
The UK’s eating disorder charity. Founded in 1989 as the Eating Disorders Association, our mission is to end the pain and suffering caused by eating disorders.

We work with young people, parents and carers, schools, colleges, universities and employers. All our work is based on sound evidence. It gives people the confidence and skills to look after their mental health.
Connection - a 24/7 mental health helpline 0800 652 0190 – offers free 24/7 telephone access to mental health advice and support as part of Access Mental Health. When young people are struggling – with friendships, school pressures, or their mental health – parents and carers are often the first people they turn to. Even with the best intentions, it can be hard to know what to say or what steps to take next.

Behaviours That Challenge Us is for parents/carers of 5 – 11 year olds who find their child’s behaviour difficult to manage at times. Presented by a Child Clinical Psychologist, to help you support and understand your child's challenges and difficulties and learn more about brain development.
Family Lives run online parenting courses for families with children at primary school or younger.
Action for Children has a fantastic parenting hub for families with children of all ages offering free advice and resources, plus a live chat service with a qualified parenting coach.
Place2Be have resources covering many aspects of mental health and wellbeing for children of primary school age as well as tips to help prepare your child move up to secondary school.
ParentLine for parents of 0 – 5’s from Dorset NHS Health Visiting team is a confidential text message service, providing advice about children’s health and development.

If you’re experiencing conflict with your partner or ex:
Whether you are living together or not, if your relationship has broken down and there are frequent unresolved arguments, it’s more likely that your child may become upset, anxious or angry and this can be reflected in their behaviour or attitude towards you or your partner. For parental relationship support, visit:Support for inter-parental communication offers free counselling to parents to help improve communication, reduce conflict and create better outcomes for your child/children.OnePlusOne run 3 free online courses: Arguing Better, Getting it Right for Children, You, Me & Baby Too. We know that for anyone living with domestic abuse, sexual violence or stalking, getting in touch with someone to help is really hard. Taking that first step can be scary, and talking to someone you don’t know may seem strange. But we are here to help. When it’s safe and right for you, please contact one of our teams.

Aspire Adoption Services - https://aspireadoption.co.uk/ Aspire offers a range of support services to all parties connected with adoption including families who have adopted, adopted adults and birth families. We also offer support services to families created through special guardianship. In addition to specialist support services, Aspire provides social events, support groups, training and contact services. Email: enquiries@aspireadoption.co.uk

Safer Schools Team https://www.dorset.police.uk/police-forces/dorset-police/areas/about-us/local-support-and-guidance/ssct-young-people/ The Safer Schools and Communities Team is a partnership between Dorset Police and Dorset Combined Youth Offending Service with a remit to provide targeted interventions to prevent and reduce anti-social behaviour, crime, and wrong-doing amongst children and young people and help keep them safe in a digital world.

About our school
Our aim is to enable all students to lead a successful, active, happy and fulfilling school life. Our students know that if they show respect for each other and themselves, make the commitment to put in effort, have positive attitudes, and persevere when learning or situations challenge them, then they will reap the rewards of their efforts. We wish to provide every student with a sense of belonging and of being valued as an individual.
Sixth-form students play an active role in school life and the transition from Year 6 to 7 through the Student Leadership Team. Their duties range from supporting our open evenings to leading our popular student forum. They are excellent role-models for our younger students and play an active role in the transition process, from visiting primary schools to talk to Year 6 to supporting clubs and events in Year 7.
We are proud of the wide range of clubs and activities that we offer outside of the curriculum—from coding and debate to climate club and performing arts. We actively encourage all Year 7s to join lunchtime or afterschool clubs to add to their enjoyment of school, learn new skills and make new connections.

Enrolling at The Blandford School
Parents and carers need to apply through Dorset Council before the end of October, and families will hear about school place offers in March. We will send information about the transition process at The Blandford School shortly after this.
https://www.dorsetcouncil.gov.uk/w/starting-secondary-or-upper-school
Preparing for secondary school
We work closely with our primary schools throughout Year 6 to help students become familiar, excited and reassured about The Blandford School before they start.
We hold a range of workshops throughout the year, some during the school day and others after school, giving Year 6 students the chance to meet staff, explore the site, and experience aspects of secondary school life. Look out for details of these events through our ongoing communication with the primary schools.
In June, our Head of Year 7 visits each primary school to talk to Year 6 students in their classroom about what to expect and to answer questions.
In July, our new students attend a Transition Day, where they meet their new tutor group and tutor. This is their first full day at The Blandford School during which they experience a range of subjects. Students go home with a photo of their new tutor group and lots of stories to tell. We also host a Transition Evening for parents and carers in July, providing information and answering any questions before the start of term.
We hold an additional Transition Day for students who are on their primary school Special Educational Needs register to ensure they are familiar with our site and key staff.

The Blandford School Community Completes Epic LEJOG Challenge and Celebrates with Family Day
Students, staff, families and the wider community come together for a remarkable challenge supporting two important charities
The Blandford School community has successfully completed its ambitious TBS Does LEJOG Challenge, bringing together students, staff, families and the wider community in an incredible display of teamwork, determination and community spirit.
The challenge saw participants collectively complete the equivalent distance from Land’s End to John o’ Groats, with people walking, running and cycling throughout the event. The original target was to cover 1,400 kilometres, but thanks to the incredible commitment of everyone involved, the community went above and beyond, completing an outstanding 2,026 kilometres.
The achievement demonstrated the enthusiasm, resilience and determination of everyone who took part, with students, staff, families and friends all playing their part in helping the school travel the distance and reach this amazing milestone.
The challenge was organised to encourage people of all ages and abilities to get active, work together and achieve something extraordinary as a school community, while also raising money and awareness for two very important charities — Teddy20, which supports children and families affected by cancer, and Andy’s Man Club, which provides a safe space for men to talk openly and access support around mental health.
Throughout the challenge, participants supported one another, celebrated milestones and showed that every contribution counted. A special highlight was the 7km turning point at The Black Cat Café, Gains Cross, where participants were welcomed, looked after and encouraged by the team. Their generosity and hospitality provided a fantastic boost for everyone taking part and helped make the journey even more memorable.
The success of the event was made possible through the dedication of the school’s PE department, with particular thanks to Head of PE, Niall Clinton, for bringing the challenge to life and inspiring the whole school community to get involved.
The fundraising pages remain open for those wishing to support these fantastic causes:
TBS Does LEJOG 2026 – Teddy20 fundraising page:https://www.justgiving.com/page/tbsdoes26teddy20
TBS Does LEJOG 2026 – Andy’s Man Club fundraising page:https://www.justgiving.com/page/theblandfordschool-tbsdoes26andysmanclub
A Family Day to Remember
To celebrate completing the challenge, The Blandford School hosted a Family Day, bringing students, families, staff and the wider community together for a fantastic day of entertainment, activities and celebration.
The event was made even more special thanks to the incredible generosity of local businesses, who supported a fantastic raffle with a wide range of prizes. A particular highlight was the opportunity to win two England v Spain tickets at Wembley, generously donated by Riverside Travel, which created huge excitement among attendees.
Visitors were also treated to an exciting preview of “Spectacular – A Night at the Musicals”, the school’s upcoming production in October 2026, with students showcasing the incredible talent and creativity within Blandford Performing Arts.
The day was filled with live music and performances, with the Stour Valley Band and Circus of Thieves providing fantastic entertainment throughout the event. Guests were also able to enjoy a range of workshops and performances from Phoenix Ariel, who brought energy, creativity and excitement to the day.
The Family Day was a wonderful celebration of everything that makes The Blandford School community so special — showcasing the talents of our students, the support of local organisations and the incredible contribution of families, staff and community partners.
The event was captured beautifully by Rob Young of RY Images, who generously donated his time and expertise by taking fantastic photographs of the day completely free of charge. His images have helped preserve the memories of this incredible community achievement.
A spokesperson for The Blandford School said:
"The LEJOG Challenge has been an incredible example of what can be achieved when our community comes together. The determination, enthusiasm and support shown by students, staff, families and our local partners has been truly inspiring. We set out to complete 1,400 kilometres and to finish on 2,026 kilometres is an amazing achievement. The Family Day was the perfect way to celebrate, bringing everyone together to enjoy performances, activities and the amazing talents within our community."
The Blandford School would like to thank everyone who participated, volunteered, donated and supported the event — including The Black Cat Café, Riverside Travel, Phoenix Ariel, Stour Valley Band, Circus of Thieves, Rob Young of RY Images and all the local businesses who contributed raffle prizes.
Together, the community has shown that with teamwork, determination and a shared purpose, we really can go the extra mile.
